chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is nothing in the heavens but they ask Allāh to permit them to visit al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him); a group descends and a group ascends.'
ai.seo_question: What do the inhabitants of the heavens ask God regarding Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the cosmic significance of Ziyarat al-Husayn, portraying it as a universal desire among the inhabitants of the heavens. The imagery of angels descending and ascending in groups underscores the continuous, active reverence of the celestial realm for the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn, elevating his shrine to a focal point of divine attention and spiritual connection.
